data.narrative:
Mindgrove Technologies is a Series A semiconductor company founded by Shashwath TR and Sharan Srinivas J, which has raised ₹85 Cr (~$10M) to date. The Chips & Semiconductors sector includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers spanning stages and valuations, though narrower peer subsets are thin.

Of three valuation methods examined, only Stage-Progression was executable. This method applies a 2.0x multiplier to the $10M total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation, yielding a $20M implied valuation. Peer-Median analysis could not be applied: while 12 same-sector peers exist, filtering for identical stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tiers returned fewer than 3 datapoints, making a statistically reliable median calculation infeasible. Public-Comp Anchoring was inapplicable due to absence of disclosed revenue; the sector median P/S of 21.5x across public semiconductors cannot be applied without target revenue data.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $17M–$23M, centered at $20M, derived solely from stage-progression mechanics. This range is narrow and rests on a single method, reflecting limited data availability rather than convergent evidence across multiple approaches. Key uncertainties include product-market traction (not provided), R&D efficiency relative to peers, and whether the $10M raise represents a post-money or pre-money figure, each of which could materially shift the fair valuation.
